note: Verdicts a human reached about sites the automatic attribution in tools/attrib.py
would not decide on its own. A site with no attribution is never patched, so this
file is the only way a reviewed site enters a patch set -- and the only way a site
the tool suspects is deliberately kept out of one.
verdict 'copy' -- the base register is the mode copy, not the edit block. The
displacement lands inside an edit-block array range purely by value. Never patch:
moving it would corrupt an unrelated field of a different object.
verdict 'junk' -- the bytes are not code, or the displacement is the function's own
jump table. Never patch.
verdict 'edit' -- confirmed edit-block reference. Patched like an automatic one.

verdict 'size' -- the constant is an array's byte size, not a base. In this block each array starts where the previous one ends, so a size and the next base are the same number. Carries `array`: the array whose size it is, which is the cap whose change would require patching it.
The regulation array's 306 reviewed sites were settled in one pass, on an argument that
is about the displacement rather than about each function. A site is called an edit-block
reference when its displacement is exactly the array base 0xc12e9c, or that base plus a
whole number of 0x314-byte records plus a field offset -- an exact landing, not a range
hit -- and when no array base minus any of the 77 measured mode-copy field offsets equals
that displacement, which is what would otherwise let a pre-biased reference to a
different array masquerade as one of these. 301 of the 306 then corroborate themselves:
the function holding them also reads the regulation count at 0xd0bcf4, so the pair is the
familiar walk-the-array idiom. The other five were read by hand.

The match table's 146 reviewed sites (rec596, 0xe9ff08, 13000 x 0x254) were settled by the same argument on 2026-09-11: a real access is the base plus a field offset below 0x254 with the record index in a register, and 40 sites are exactly that, in the block accessor functions and the copy routines; the 106 others land on a record in the thousands by value, and are mode-object fields (verdict copy) or bytes that are not code (verdict junk).
